Definition: The vertical distance between baselines of successive lines of text. Named after the strips of lead used in hot-metal typesetting.
The adjustment of space between a specific pair of characters.
Uniform adjustment of spacing across a range of characters.
Printed content that extends beyond the trim edge so no white edge remains after cutting.
The space between columns, or the inner margin where pages meet at the spine.

A short last line of a paragraph left alone at the top of a column.

Editors usually fix widows by adjusting tracking or rewording.
